title: Magnetic permeability and zone-folded phonons in layered NiPS$_3$
authors: André A. A. Silva, Eduardo D. Stefanato, Nicolas M. Kawahala, Flávio H. Feres, João Vítor T. P. Vital, Bernardo R. A. Neves, Jan Plutnar, Zdenek Sofer, Ana C. F. Brito, Felix G. G. Hernandez, Raul O. Freitas
abstract: Nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS$_3$) stands out as a Mott insulator exhibiting XY-type antiferromagnetic order. In this work, we investigate the electrodynamic response of single-crystalline NiPS$_3$ using Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) as a function of temperature. In cases where the magnetic permeability cannot be approximated to unity, conventional THz transmission analysis is often restricted to the complex refractive index, hindering the distinction between magnetic and dielectric contributions. To overcome this limitation, we demonstrate an extraction methodology capable of decoupling the magnetic permeability from the electric permittivity. Assuming that the dielectric contribution remains invariant below the N'eel temperature (TN), we used data from the paramagnetic phase to isolate the intrinsic magnetic component at 13 K. The angular and thermal dependence of the spectra revealed a magnon mode near 1 THz (for 0$^\circ$ orientation) and, distinctively, a zone-folded phonon activated by symmetry breaking (at 90$^\circ$). The isolated magnetic permeability was successfully modeled using Drude-Lorentz oscillators, enabling the extraction of fundamental spin dynamics parameters in this material.
summary: This paper uses Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy on $	ext{NiPS}_3$ to overcome limitations in separating magnetic and dielectric responses. By assuming the dielectric constant is stable upon cooling, the authors successfully isolate the magnetic permeability. This allowed them to distinguish between a temperature-dependent magnon mode and a symmetry-breaking zone-folded phonon, providing fundamental spin dynamics parameters.
main_problem: The study aims to investigate the electrodynamic response of $	ext{NiPS}_3$ to decouple the magnetic permeability ($\mu$) from the electric permittivity ($\epsilon$) in the Terahertz (THz) range.
main_result: The research successfully identified a magnon mode near $1 	ext{ THz}$ (temperature-dependent) and a distinct zone-folded phonon activated by symmetry breaking (temperature-independent) using THz-TDS.
method: The authors developed an extraction methodology using THz-TDS data, assuming the dielectric contribution ($\epsilon$) is invariant below the Néel temperature ($T_N$), allowing $\mu(\omega)$ to be isolated.
model_or_system: The physical system is single-crystalline $	ext{NiPS}_3$, a layered Mott insulator exhibiting XY-type antiferromagnetic order. Measurements are performed using THz-TDS across different crystal orientations ($0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$) and temperatures.
key_observables: Complex permittivity ($\epsilon(\omega)$), complex permeability ($\mu(\omega)$), magnon mode resonance, and zone-folded phonon resonance.
important_parameters: Temperature ($13 	ext{ K}$ to $300 	ext{ K}$), THz frequency ($\sim 1 	ext{ THz}$), and crystallographic orientation ($0^\circ$ vs $90^\circ$).
main_assumptions: The dielectric contribution ($\epsilon$) is assumed to remain invariant when cooling below the Néel temperature ($T_N$), and the magnetic permeability can be modeled using Drude-Lorentz oscillators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural characterization, anisotropic dielectric measurements, and dispersion plots showing temperature-dependent magnon shifts ($0^\circ$) versus constant phonon frequencies ($90^\circ$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the limitation of conventional THz analysis, introduces the decoupling methodology, presents THz-TDS measurements at varying temperatures and orientations, and finally models the isolated magnetic permeability using Drude-Lorentz oscillators to extract spin dynamics parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated experimental technique to probe coupled magnetic and lattice excitations in quantum materials, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
